questions.question: What software architecture pattern in HCI divides a system into three distinct parts: Model, View, and Controller?
What is the primary purpose of using the Model-View-Controller (MVC) design pattern?
questions.answer: To make programs easier to build, understand, and fix

questions.question: Which component of MVC is described as the 'brain' of the system, managing data and logic?
Which component of MVC represents the 'face' of the system, showing what the user sees?
Which component of MVC represents the 'hands' of the system, handling what the user does?
In the restaurant analogy for MVC, what role corresponds to the Model?
In the restaurant analogy for MVC, what role corresponds to the View?
In the restaurant analogy for MVC, what role corresponds to the Controller?
Which component of MVC stores and manages the system's data and rules?
Which MVC component updates data when something changes but does not care about how things look on screen?
What happens to a program if it lacks a Model component?
questions.answer: The program has no knowledge to show

questions.question: Which component of MVC serves as the visual representation of the data?
Which component of MVC changes automatically when the Model updates?
What problem occurs if a program does not have a View component?
questions.answer: Users can't see or interact with the data

questions.question: Which MVC component acts as a bridge between the user and the system?
Which component of MVC takes input from the user (such as clicks, taps, voice, or typing)?
Which component of MVC decides what action to perform and tells the Model or View what to do?
What limitation occurs if a system does not have a Controller?
questions.answer: The user cannot communicate with the system

questions.question: Enumerate two functions of the View component.
answers: Shows information to the user in a friendly way
Changes automatically when the Model updates

answers: Takes input from the user (clicks, taps, voice, typing)
Tells the Model or View what to do

questions.question: Enumerate four user input examples handled by the Controller.
Enumerate the four steps of how MVC works together in order.
answers: User does something (click, tap, type) -> handled by Controller
Model notifies the View of changes
View shows the updated information to the User

answers: Shows information in a friendly way

Together they make the system run smoothly

questions.question: Enumerate the two destinations the waiter in the restaurant analogy delivers orders between.
Enumerate the two components involved when the Controller tells them what to do after deciding an action.
What quality describes how easy, efficient, and effective a system is to use?
Which aspect of usability is measured through performance tasks such as click counts or completion times?
Which aspect of usability is based on user opinions, feedback, and surveys regarding how simple or tiring a system feels?
What evaluation tool often includes questions involving ease of use, ease of learning, fatigue, and simple preference?
What concept refers to the overall feeling, satisfaction, and emotional connection users have while interacting with a system?
What dimension of evaluation covers how enjoyable, intuitive, and stress-free an application feels?
What is described as the simplest evaluation method involving talking to users or watching them use the system?
Which evaluation method helps identify problems that designers might miss by directly talking to or observing users?
In which evaluation method do users "think aloud" while using the system, describing what they are doing and why?
Which evaluation method reveals users' thought processes and points of confusion as they describe their actions in real time?
What method involves usability experts reviewing a system using established principles?
What are the established design principles used by usability experts during an evaluation called?
Who created the ten General UI heuristics widely used in expert heuristic evaluation?
Which Nielsen heuristic requires that the system always keep users informed about system status through appropriate feedback?
Which Nielsen heuristic specifies that the system should speak the users' language with familiar words, phrases, and concepts?
questions.answer: Match between system and the real world

questions.question: Which Nielsen heuristic provides users with an "emergency exit" to leave unwanted states without extended dialogue?
Which Nielsen heuristic ensures that users do not have to wonder whether different words, situations, or actions mean the same thing?
Which Nielsen heuristic focuses on careful design that prevents a problem from occurring in the first place?
Which Nielsen heuristic emphasizes making objects, actions, and options visible so users do not have to remember information across dialogues?
Which Nielsen heuristic allows shortcuts to speed up interaction for expert users while accommodating inexperienced users?
Which Nielsen heuristic states that dialogues should not contain information that is irrelevant or rarely needed?
Which Nielsen heuristic states that error messages should be expressed in plain language, indicate the problem, and suggest a solution?
questions.answer: Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors

Which principle requires evaluations to be respectful, safe, and protective of participants' well-being?
What specific performance metric counts user selection actions to complete a given task?
What quantitative usability metric tracks how long a participant takes to complete an action?
What qualitative survey metric evaluates physical or mental weariness resulting from interface interaction?
Which evaluation goal ensures that the overall interaction with the system is positive and enjoyable?
What form of data includes satisfaction scores, task times, and error rates to quantify system performance?
What quality ensures that the entire evaluation process focuses on the rights, safety, and comfort of the user?
Which real-time technique asks users to articulate their actions while navigating a system to highlight confusion?
What observation technique involves directly watching users interact with an interface to discover unstated issues?
Enumerate the two main criteria for evaluating human-computer interaction.
Enumerate the two forms of usability measurements.
